mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% in a single month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and dampens earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and retail sales (implied by HOUST) over two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth outpacing GDP growth over six months) signals elevated precautionary savings and lower marginal propensity to consume, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth exceeds GDPC1 growth for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS growth exceeds GDPC1 growth for six consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
